mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in a month is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to higher discounting of expected corporate cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in a single month
regime_hint: tightening cycle after a period of easing
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the same month of rate hikes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly employment (PAYEMS) coinciding with falling unemployment (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market, which precedes a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE decreases over the same month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative despite the labor signal persists for at least 3 months (Granger causality fails).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 2% predicts a negative S&P 500 5-day forward return as it indicates weakening economic momentum.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >2% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically significant (p > 0.10) during such declines.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 3% for two months is expected to precede a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as it signals policy tightening anticipation.
failure_condition: No significant positive 20-day forward return occurs during such inflation episodes (95% CI includes zero).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in residential housing starts (HOUST) below 1000 units in a month, combined with rising unemployment (UNRATE), creates a contrarian signal that predicts a positive S&P 500 20-day return.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < 1000 and UNRATE rises in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain negative despite the signal persists for at least 4 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden surge in job openings (PAYEMS) exceeding 200,000 in a month without a corresponding drop in unemployment (UNRATE) suggests labor market imbalances and precedes a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 200,000 and UNRATE remains flat or falls in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during such events.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in retail sales (not available in catalog; fallback: use GDPC1 as a proxy for broad demand) of 5% over two months predicts a negative S&P 500 5-day forward return due to weak consumer demand.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls by >5% over two consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during such declines.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the 10-year yield proxy (FEDFUNDS > 4%) for three consecutive months is expected to produce a positive S&P 20-day forward return as investors anticipate rate cuts.
regime_hint: yield curve flattening and rate-cut expectations
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.10) during such periods.
